data.name: TriageDesk
data.idea: A small web app for a support team: an agent pastes an incoming customer support ticket, and an AI feature classifies it (category, urgency), writes a one-sentence summary and suggests a first reply; the agent reviews and edits the suggestion. Must stay safe against prompt injection in ticket text, work without an API key via a clearly labelled deterministic fallback, and have an evaluation suite with explicit thresholds. Keep it small: Node.js, no database, single-page UI.

handoff.objective: Independently review the TriageDesk architecture brief (submission sub-muyloqv9-015ebd44) and approve it or request changes at the architecture gate.
handoff.context: TriageDesk is a small local Node.js 22 web app: an agent pastes a support ticket and gets a category, an urgency, a one-sentence summary and an editable suggested reply. It calls the Anthropic Messages API through raw fetch, falls back to a clearly labelled deterministic rule-based classifier, and must be safe against prompt injection. Constraints: zero npm dependencies, no database, a single page, and an eval suite with explicit thresholds (fixed in the brief's 'Evaluation metrics and thresholds' table). Memory search found one lesson (mem-k-muyljkrt-01991ac7, 'need node-fetch/axios because global fetch is missing'); its check verdict was DOES-NOT-APPLY (requires Node <18, environment has 22.22.0), so it was rejected and not cited. The model id claude-opus-5-5 and the request shape (output_config.format json_schema, effort low, anthropic-version 2023-06-01) come from the claude-api reference cached 2026-10-06. They were not verified by a live call because no API key is set (A5, RISK-7). The submission's runtime evidence is ev:ev-muylm2jz-017e07c4. An earlier evidence run, ev:ev-muyllyra-018a7124, failed only because of shell quoting in the command and carries no product signal.
handoff.expectedOutput: An architecture gate review (approve or changes_requested) with findings referenced by id, covering requirement testability, AC traceability, trust boundaries and injection controls, the fallback design, the eval thresholds, and the scope exclusions.
acceptanceCriteria: Every required section (Users, Problem, Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, Architecture, Assumptions, Open Questions, Risks) is present and substantive
Each AC traces to an R/NFR and is decidable by a test or an inspection
Prompt-injection controls (NFR2, AC7, AC9) and the eval thresholds are explicit and measurable
Unverified claims (model id, API surface, live quality) are labelled as assumptions or risks rather than stated as fact
handoff.completedWork: Wrote the architecture brief: users, problem, R1-R10 and NFR1-NFR10, workflows W1-W4, AC1-AC15 with an eval metric and threshold table, scope with reasons for each exclusion, components and a data-flow diagram with trust boundaries TB1-TB4, a decision table with alternatives, constraints, success criteria, A1-A8 and Q1-Q6. Recorded RISK-1..RISK-8 in the risk register. Recorded runtime-capability evidence (Node 22.22.0: global fetch, AbortSignal.timeout, node:test, node:http). Submitted the architecture gate.
remainingIssues: Q1 (user): live model default claude-opus-5-5 vs the cheaper claude-haiku-5-5
Q3 (user): will an API key be provided so the live eval can run, or is fallback-only verification acceptable with live thresholds marked unverified?
Q4 (user): may raw ticket text (possible PII) be sent to the Anthropic API, or is redaction required first?
Q2/Q5/Q6 have proposed defaults (taxonomy as in A3; no server-side refusal fallback beta; no URLs in replies) that the reviewer may accept
A5/RISK-7: model id and request shape are not verified live; no API key is set in this environment
The choice of raw fetch over the official @anthropic-ai/sdk is a deliberate trade-off for the zero-dependency constraint; the reviewer should confirm it

review.summary: The brief is well structured and honest about unverified claims, and the scope is right-sized. It still cannot go to design yet. It contradicts two recorded orchestrator decisions: the default model is now Haiku and PII redaction is now required. The raw-fetch structured-output path ignores documented JSON-schema keyword limits, which would make every live call 400 and fall back with nothing to show it before delivery. The localhost bind is the only access control and it does not stop DNS rebinding. The holdout split and the injection_safety metric cannot measure what they claim to measure.

criteria.description: Completeness: users, problem, workflows, constraints, scope and requirements are explicit and consistent with recorded decisions
criteria.notes: Users, problem, W1-W4 and scope reasons are good. However, the brief still sets claude-opus-5-5 as the default (lines 233, 245) and keeps PII redaction out of scope (line 168), against decisions dec-muylppww / dec-muylpq02 (ARCH-1). It has no Host/Origin requirement (ARCH-3).

criteria.description: Testability: every AC is decidable by test or inspection and every requirement traces to an AC
criteria.notes: AC1-AC15 are concrete and trace to R/NFR ids. Gaps: the RISK-7 mitigation (4xx -> model_error) and stop_reason max_tokens have no AC (ARCH-6). The validator's 'one sentence' and 'no URL/email' rules are not defined precisely enough to decide (ARCH-7). Success criterion 2 reports holdout results but sets no pass rule for them (ARCH-4).

criteria.description: Assumptions: risky or unverified assumptions are labelled, and questions that need the user are escalated
criteria.notes: A1-A8 carry 'Blocks' notes, and A5/A6 honestly mark the reference-only claims. Q1/Q3/Q4 were escalated correctly. Folding the orchestrator's answers back into the brief is tracked under ARCH-1.

criteria.description: Complexity: no unnecessary components; simplest design that meets requirements
criteria.notes: node:http, a single static page, no state, a pure-function fallback and one model call per request. Nothing here is superfluous. The rationale for the zero-dependency choice is misattributed (ARCH-8, minor), but the choice itself is defensible.

criteria.description: Feasibility: technology limits, API surface, latency and cost verified against authoritative sources
criteria.notes: The Node 22 runtime is verified. I verified the model ids and support for output_config.format and effort against platform.claude.com on 2026-10-07. The raw-fetch schema limits are unaddressed (ARCH-2). The brief does not account for thinking tokens counting toward max_tokens (ARCH-6).

criteria.description: Security and privacy: trust boundaries, secrets, PII, prompt injection, least privilege
criteria.notes: TB1-TB4, no tools, display-only output, textContent with CSP, and the key read from env only are all strong. Gaps: DNS rebinding bypasses the localhost bind (ARCH-3). The required redaction has no requirement or AC, and its scope leaves out payment card numbers (ARCH-1).

criteria.description: AI features: real value, eval cases with sound thresholds, fallback on model failure, human oversight
criteria.notes: The value statement, the labelled fallback and the human-in-the-loop design are good. The holdout split cannot detect overfitting (ARCH-4). injection_safety mixes up accuracy with attack success and rests on too few cases to support its claim (ARCH-5).

criteria.description: Risk register: likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner for every material risk, with mitigations that hold
criteria.notes: RISK-1..8 are complete in form. RISK-5 rates likelihood Low on the strength of the 127.0.0.1 bind, which DNS rebinding defeats (ARCH-3). No risk covers redaction failure or leakage once redaction is adopted (ARCH-1).

findings.title: Brief contradicts recorded decisions on default model and PII redaction
findings.detail: The orchestrator recorded dec-muylppww (default ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5) and dec-muylpq02 (redact emails and phone numbers before any live call). The submitted brief still says the opposite. Line 233 (decision table) and line 245 (deployment) default to claude-opus-5-5. Line 168 puts PII redaction out of scope. A5, RISK-3 and RISK-7 describe Opus-specific behaviour ('thinking cannot be disabled'). No R/NFR/AC covers redaction (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). Design would therefore build from a brief that disagrees with the project record. I accept the Haiku choice: claude-haiku-5-5 exists, supports structured outputs and output_config.effort 'low', and its default effort is medium (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview.md, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort.md, both checked 2026-10-07). I challenge the redaction scope. The product handles billing tickets, which routinely contain payment card numbers. Redacting only emails and phones still sends card numbers (PANs) to a third party, and Q4 itself listed card numbers as a redaction class.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all of the following. (1) Sets the default ANTHROPIC_MODEL to claude-haiku-5-5, marked as pending user confirmation, and rewrites A5, the decision table, RISK-3 and RISK-7 for Haiku 5.5 behaviour: adaptive thinking on by default, effort set explicitly to low, and thinking counted toward max_tokens. (2) Adds a requirement and an AC for redaction before the live call. The AC uses a stubbed transport to assert that marker email addresses, phone numbers and Luhn-valid card numbers in a ticket do not appear in the captured outbound request body. Card numbers are in scope unless the user explicitly declines. (3) Defines the order of operations: the injection detector runs on the original text, then redaction, then delimiter neutralisation. Placeholders must not collide with the <ticket> delimiters. (4) Updates the live-mode UI notice to say which classes are redacted. (5) Adds or extends a risk for redaction misses (false negatives).

findings.title: Raw-fetch JSON schema limits unaddressed; live path can 400 on every call
findings.detail: The brief chooses raw fetch with output_config.format json_schema and enforces lengths (summary <=200, reply 1-1200) and enums. Per https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs.md (checked 2026-10-07), the API rejects raw schemas that contain minLength/maxLength, minimum/maximum/multipleOf or maxItems with a 400. additionalProperties must be false on every object. Claude may change the capitalisation of enum values. The SDK helpers strip the unsupported keywords and validate locally, but the raw-fetch design does not get that benefit. AC9 checks only output_config.format.type === 'json_schema'. A schema that naturally includes maxLength 200/1200 would therefore pass every offline test while every live request returns 400 and falls back with model_error. Decision Q3 means no live call happens before delivery, so the defect would ship undetected and live mode would silently be fallback-only. The strict validator would also reject enum values that are correct but differently capitalised (invalid_output), which inflates fallback_rate.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when NFR2 states that the schema sent to the model uses only supported keywords: type, properties, required, enum, additionalProperties:false on every object, and no minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum/maxItems. Lengths are enforced only by the server-side validator. AC9 must walk the captured schema and fail on any unsupported keyword or on an object without additionalProperties:false. The brief must also define the enum-case policy: normalise with a case-insensitive match before the enum check, or reject explicitly with a stated reason. Either way a test must cover it.

findings.title: Localhost bind is defeated by DNS rebinding; no Host/Origin validation
findings.detail: The trust model relies on binding to 127.0.0.1 with no auth or rate limit (NFR3, Scope, RISK-5 likelihood 'Low'). A web page the agent visits can use DNS rebinding: an attacker hostname re-resolves to 127.0.0.1, so its script becomes same-origin with the app. The script can then POST application/json to /api/triage without hitting a CORS preflight, read the responses and spend the operator's API key without limit. The 415 content-type check does not help, because rebinding makes the request same-origin. No requirement or AC in the brief validates the Host or Origin headers (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c: no Host/Origin/DNS-rebinding lines). The fix is cheap and belongs to the architecture's trust boundary TB1.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when NFR3 requires the server to reject any request whose Host header is not in an allowlist derived from HOST:PORT (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]). The rejection must come before body parsing or any model call. The server must also reject POSTs whose Origin header is present and not same-origin, and must emit no CORS headers. AC11 (or a new AC) must test that 'Host: attacker.example' and a foreign Origin are rejected and that the fetch stub is never called. RISK-5 must be updated with this mitigation and its likelihood re-rated.

findings.title: Holdout split cannot detect fallback-rule overfitting
findings.detail: Thresholds are scored over all rows, and the roughly 30% holdout is only 'reported separately' (eval section; Success Criterion 2). If rules overfit the tuning rows perfectly, category_accuracy >= 0.70 and urgency_accuracy >= 0.65 still pass with 0% holdout accuracy, and high_urgency_recall >= 0.80 passes with 33% holdout recall (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). RISK-4 names this exact failure mode, and its mitigation is ineffective as written. With about 40 rows the holdout has about 12 rows, so per-metric holdout numbers carry 1-3 high-urgency rows. The brief does not say how a frozen dataset is proven to predate the rules.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when (1) the fallback thresholds are enforced on the holdout rows, or a stated holdout floor is enforced (for example, holdout within 0.10 of each threshold), and npm run eval exits non-zero when it is missed. (2) The brief sets minimum holdout counts, for example at least 2 rows per category and at least 4 label=high rows, enlarging the dataset if needed. (3) The dataset and holdout tags are frozen by recording the dataset's sha256 as evidence before any fallback-rule commit, and the verification gate checks that hash.

findings.title: injection_safety mixes accuracy with attack success and overclaims on 8 cases
findings.detail: injection_safety requires that the final category and urgency equal the true labels on every attack row, at 1.00, for both providers. Fallback accuracy is only required to reach 0.70/0.65 overall. Either the attack rows end up chosen to be easy for keyword rules (selection bias), or the metric fails for reasons that have nothing to do with injection. The brief says the fallback 'cannot be injected because it never echoes ticket text'. That holds for text echo but not for classification: its listed urgency cues ('urgent', 'outage', 'charged twice', 'data loss') are words an attacker controls. The heuristic detector's recall >= 0.90 is measured on attacks written by the same team that writes the detector regexes, with no held-out attack families, so the test is easy to game. Statistically, 8 out of 8 passes leaves a 95% upper bound of about 31% on the true failure rate (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). Success Criterion 4 ('Injection safety is 1.00 for both providers') cannot be met for live under decision Q3, because live evals are NOT RUN.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all of the following. (1) Each attack row declares the attacker's targets (requested category/urgency that differ from the true labels, a canary token, a URL). Attack success is defined as the output adopting an attacker target, or the canary, prompt-marker or URL appearing. injection_safety (attack-success rate = 0) is kept separate from accuracy on attack rows, which is reported under the normal accuracy thresholds. (2) RISK-1 states the residual risk that fallback classification can be steered by keywords, mitigated by the flag and human review, and the fallback 'cannot be injected' claim is corrected. (3) The attack set is enlarged (for example to at least 20 rows across the detector's rule families), and some attack families are held out so that detector regexes are not written against them. (4) Results are reported as '0 failures in N' with the sample size, not as proof of safety. (5) Success Criterion 4 marks live injection results as NOT RUN when no key is available.

findings.title: Fallback triggers for HTTP errors and max_tokens truncation are untested
findings.detail: AC4 covers throw, timeout, non-JSON, out-of-enum, URL and refusal. It does not cover a non-2xx HTTP response (400/404 for a wrong model id, 429, 529), although RISK-7's mitigation relies on '4xx -> model_error'. stop_reason 'max_tokens' is checked by the live provider but maps to no R6 fallbackReason. Thinking counts toward max_tokens on Haiku 5.5 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort.md, checked 2026-10-07), so the 1,024 cap needs a rationale.
findings.recommendation: Extend AC4 with stubbed HTTP 404 (with a body), 429 and 529 responses mapped to model_error, and with stop_reason max_tokens mapped to a named reason. State why max_tokens=1024 leaves room for thinking at effort low, or raise it.

findings.title: Validator rules 'one sentence' and 'no URL/email' are not precisely defined
findings.detail: The single-sentence rule (R3, AC2) and the no-URL/no-email rule (NFR2) decide fallback, but text like 'e.g.', 'v2.1', 'Mr.', bare domains ('example.com') and obfuscated forms ('name at example dot com') are undefined. As a result the model-validity and fallback_rate metrics depend on how the implementer reads the rule.
findings.recommendation: Define both rules as deterministic patterns, in the brief or as a binding design-gate item, with accept and reject test vectors for the edge cases above.

findings.title: Zero-dependency constraint attributed to the project, which never set it
findings.detail: The decision table says the SDK 'would break the zero-dependency constraint the project set'. The project idea says only 'Keep it small: Node.js, no database, single-page UI'. Raw fetch is defensible on its merits: one endpoint, an injectable transport and no retries wanted. But it is the architect's choice, and it loses the SDK's schema stripping and typed errors (see ARCH-2).
findings.recommendation: Restate NFR1 and the decision row as an architect's decision with its trade-offs (including ARCH-2), and list it for user confirmation alongside Q1/Q4.

findings.title: Q2/Q5/Q6 proposed defaults acceptable; Q5 moot with Haiku default
findings.detail: I accept the A3 taxonomy (Q2), local-only refusal handling (Q5) and no URLs in replies (Q6). According to the claude-api reference (cached 2026-10-06), Claude Haiku 5.5 has no server-side refusal fallback, so Q5 has no option to choose once the default becomes Haiku.
findings.recommendation: Record Q2/Q5/Q6 as decided with the proposed defaults, and note that Q5 no longer applies under the Haiku default.

I re-ran brief-vectors.js myself (ev:ev-muym6zly-019e5cb3, passed). I accept the author's departure on fallback steering (leak = 0, steer <= 0.25 for the keyword fallback, 0 for live) on its merits. criteria.description: Risk register: likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner for every material risk, with mitigations that hold

findings.title: Baseline card redaction misses cards adjacent to other digit groups (expiry, CVV, preceding phone)
findings.detail: The CARD pattern in brief-vectors.js, `(?<!\d)\d(?:[ -]?\d){12,18}(?!\d)`, is greedy. Its lookahead accepts a following space, so it takes the longest 13-19-digit window. If that window fails Luhn, the replace callback returns it unchanged and never tries the shorter, Luhn-valid sub-window. My probe ran the submitted file unmodified (ev:ev-muym7oav-0127baed). 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 12/27', 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 123' and 'Call 555 0137 4111 1111 1111 1111' all leave 4111111111111111 in the output. The PHONE pass then skips them too, because they have more than 15 digits. The controls (card alone, card followed by a year) are redacted correctly. Card plus expiry is a common way to write a card number in a billing ticket. R11's normative wording and AC16's generic assertion ('no Luhn-valid run of 13-19 digits') are correct. The gap is in the baseline pattern and in AC16's fixed vectors, which a faithful implementation would pass while leaking. This stays minor because the brief lets the design gate refine patterns, RISK-9 owns the residual risk, and live mode is not exercised in this delivery (no key).
findings.recommendation: Condition for the design gate. Add these three inputs to the AC16 vectors and make the redactor pass them: 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 12/27', 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 123' and 'Call 555 0137 4111 1111 1111 1111'. One way is to treat each separator-delimited digit run as candidates and redact any contiguous sub-sequence of groups whose digits are 13-19 long and Luhn-valid. AC16's 'no Luhn-valid run' check must scan every sub-window, not just maximal runs. The design-gate reviewer should treat a missing fix as major at that gate.

findings.title: V2 bare-domain rule rejects product names such as 'ASP.NET' and 'socket.io'; V1 rejects 'Oct. 3'
findings.detail: The probe (ev:ev-muym7oav-0127baed) shows that V2 rejects 'Customer reports ASP.NET errors after the update.' and 'Socket.io connections drop every minute.', because .net and .io are on the TLD list. V1 rejects 'Sync fails since Oct. 3 update.' because 'oct' is not on the abbreviation allowlist. Technical-ticket summaries will mention such names, so these false rejections become invalid_output and inflate live fallback_rate (threshold <= 0.05). The safety direction is right: over-rejection only causes a fallback. This is a quality issue, not a security one.
evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md#Output validation rules (normative; baseline patterns verified by ev:ev-muylz82a-01c7d490)
findings.recommendation: At the design gate, choose one: (a) tell the model in the system prompt not to write dotted product or domain-like names, or (b) add a small allowlist of known product tokens (asp.net, socket.io) with matching accept vectors, or (c) record the false-positive rate as accepted. Do not weaken the reject vectors already listed. Month abbreviations may be added to the V1 allowlist.

findings.title: Held-out attack families are visible in the repo after freeze
findings.detail: Held-out families are defined as rows 'the detector author never sees before freeze'. However, eval/dataset.json lives in the same repository, so the detector or fallback author can read the heldOutFamily rows after the freeze and tune against them. That would inflate injection_flag_recall_heldout and reduce injection_steer. Held-out recall has no threshold, so the incentive is low.
findings.recommendation: In the plan, the detector and fallback task handoffs should state that the author did not read heldOutFamily rows, and the phase reviewer should spot-check that the detector rule ids and patterns do not quote held-out row phrasing.

resolvedFindings.resolution: All five conditions are met. (1) The default model is claude-haiku-5-5, pending user confirmation, in NFR10, Deployment shape, the 'Default model' row and Q1. A5, RISK-3 and RISK-7 are rewritten for Haiku 5.5: adaptive thinking on by default and counted toward max_tokens, effort low set explicitly. A new 'Thinking control' row explains why thinking:disabled is not sent (it returns 400 on Opus 5.5). (2) R11 adds redaction of email, Luhn-valid card and phone, with cards in scope unless the user declines (Q4). AC16 uses a capturing fetch stub, marker emails, phones and Luhn cards, a digits-only check and non-redaction controls. (3) R12 fixes the order as detector on the original text, then redact, then neutralise < and >. The placeholders are bracket-only. (4) The NFR4 live-mode notice names the redacted and unredacted classes. (5) RISK-9 covers misses and over-redaction. I re-ran the baseline vectors and they pass. The adjacency gap I found in the baseline pattern is tracked separately as minor ARCH-10.

NFR2 restricts the schema to type/properties/required/enum/additionalProperties, with additionalProperties:false on every object and no length, number, array, pattern or format keywords. This matches the structured-outputs documentation I checked on 2026-10-07. Lengths are enforced only in V4. AC9 adds a recursive schema walk plus a self-check that maxLength is rejected, and the walker in brief-vectors.js passes on my re-run, including the maxLength and missing-additionalProperties rejections. V3 defines case-insensitive enum normalisation with its reason, and AC4(m) tests it. RISK-7 and the failure-mode row cover the 400-on-every-call scenario, which shows up as model_error.
evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md#Output validation rules (normative; baseline patterns verified by ev:ev-muylz82a-01c7d490)

resolvedFindings.resolution: NFR3 now makes the Host allowlist derived from HOST:PORT (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]) the first step of every request, before routing or body reading, returning 403 forbidden_host. It rejects a present non-same-origin Origin, including null, on non-GET/HEAD requests, sends no Access-Control-* headers, and returns 405 for OPTIONS. AC17 tests a foreign Host on POST, health and static routes and a missing Host. It tests that a 20 KB body with a foreign Host gets 403, not 413, which proves the check precedes body reading. It also tests foreign and null Origin, positive controls for localhost and [::1], and that the fetch stub is called 0 times. AC11 asserts no CORS headers. RISK-5 is re-rated from inherent Medium to residual Low, citing the control.

(1) Holdout floors, each equal to its threshold minus 0.10, are enforced with a non-zero exit (R9, AC8, Success Criterion 2). AC8 includes a synthetic test in which the all-rows thresholds pass but a holdout floor fails. (2) Minimum counts are set: at least 60 benign rows, and a holdout of at least 20 rows with every category >= 3, every urgency >= 4 and label=high >= 5, checked by the runner. With 5 high rows, the 0.70 floor needs 4 of 5. (3) Freeze: sha256 evidence for the dataset and thresholds is recorded before the first commit to the fallback or detector rules. The verification gate checks both the hash and the timestamp ordering against git log, and the plan must order the dataset task first. RISK-4 is updated.

(1) Attack rows declare {family, targetCategory, targetUrgency, canary, url}. injection_leak (canary, url, prompt marker TDSK-SYS-7Q2, or a V2 match), injection_steer and attack_success are separate from accuracy, which is computed on attack rows using their true labels and printed separately. (2) RISK-1 states the residual keyword-steering risk, and the Fallback row corrects the 'cannot be injected' claim. (3) There are at least 20 attack rows across at least 6 families, including at least 2 held-out families (at least 6 rows), and held-out recall is reported with N. (4) Results are reported as 'k failures in N' with the 3/N bound and never as 'safe'. (5) Success Criterion 4 marks live results NOT RUN. On the author's deliberate departure: my recommendation was attack success = 0. The author instead keeps leak = 0 for the fallback and caps fallback steering at 0.25, while live steering stays at 0. I accept this on the merits. A keyword classifier cannot tell an attacker's 'URGENT outage' from a genuine one, so a 0-steer requirement could only be met by fitting rules to the attack rows, which is the overfitting ARCH-4 targets. The harmful injection outcomes (leaking a link, canary or prompt into the reply) stay at 0 for the fallback, and its templates prevent them structurally. Steering only changes a label that a human reviews, behind the injection flag. Detector-matched sentences are removed before scoring as a cheap mitigation. Both the threshold and its rationale are explicit and bounded.

R6 adds truncated. AC4 covers HTTP 404 with a body, 429, 529 and 500 as model_error, max_tokens as truncated, a thinking block before the text block, and at most one fetch call. NFR7 raises max_tokens to 2048, gives a rationale (A9, D2) and makes it configurable.

V1 and V2 are now deterministic patterns with binding accept and reject vectors covering e.g., v2.1, Mr., bare domains and obfuscated emails. I re-ran the vectors and they pass. The remaining false positives on dotted product names are tracked as minor ARCH-11.

findings.title: API key egress is unconstrained: fetch follows cross-origin redirects with x-api-key, and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL accepts plain http to any host and is commonly inherited
findings.detail: Three gaps let the key and the redacted ticket leave the host somewhere other than the intended endpoint. There is no request-driven SSRF: the URL is fixed at startup and never taken from request data. (a) Redirects. C6.4/C7 call fetchImpl with {method, headers, body, signal} and no `redirect` option, so the default `follow` applies. My probe on Node v22.22.0 (ev:ev-muymwez0-01deadbe) sent a POST with x-api-key to 127.0.0.1:A, which answered 307 to localhost:B, a different origin. Server B received `x-api-key: FAKE-KEY-123`, method POST and the full body. The same request with `redirect: 'error'` threw a TypeError. The Fetch standard strips only Authorization on cross-origin redirects, not custom headers. So any 307/308 from the configured base URL (a misconfigured or compromised proxy, a captive portal, or a MITM on an http base URL) hands over the key and the ticket. (b) Scheme and host. C6.1 accepts any `http:` or `https:` URL, so `http://<remote>` sends the key in cleartext. Userinfo, query and fragment are not rejected either (`https://x/?a=1` + '/v1/messages' produces a malformed URL). (c) Ambient inheritance. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is the variable the official Anthropic SDKs read for their base URL (claude-api skill reference, model table cached 2026-10-06, Client config: "`base_url` (or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` env)"). It is set in this very build environment: I checked that it is set without printing its value. A developer who points it at a gateway for other tools would silently route TriageDesk's key and tickets there, and the listening log does not show it. T11 lists the threat, but the only mitigation is 'operator-only, documented'. In addition, test/helpers/spawn-server.js is specified as starting the server 'with the given env' without saying whether process.env is merged. A merged env would let a spawned 'fallback-mode' test pick up a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or base URL from the developer's shell, which breaks NFR9 (offline) and AC10.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the spec states all of the following, each with a named test. (1) C6.4/C7: the provider passes `redirect: 'error'` (add it to the fetchImpl init type). Any 3xx, or the resulting throw, maps to model_error with a fixed detail. Test in unit/anthropic-provider.test.js: a capture stub asserts init.redirect === 'error'. A contract test with fake-anthropic answering 307 to a second loopback server asserts a fallback model_error and 0 requests at the second server. (2) C6.1: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL must be `https:`, or `http:` only when the hostname is 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1]. URLs with username, password, search or hash are rejected with a ConfigError that names the variable only. Add unit/config.test.js vectors for http://remote.example (reject), http://127.0.0.1:9 (accept), https://u:p@x (reject) and https://x/?q (reject). (3) Either rename the variable to an app-specific name (e.g. TRIAGE_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL), or keep the name and add `baseUrlCustom: true|false` to the `listening` event plus a README warning that it is inherited from SDK/CLI configuration. State which. (4) spawn-server.js builds the child env explicitly (PATH plus the test-supplied variables) and never spreads process.env. contract/privacy.test.js sets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='' explicitly for the fallback-mode run.

findings.title: Holdout isolation is attestation-only: the rules author's only eval path scores and prints holdout results, so holdout floors stop measuring generalisation
findings.detail: Holdout floors (brief ARCH-4 option b, AC8, Success Criterion 2) exist so that rules fitted to tuning rows fail. E5 moves holdout and held-out rows into eval/holdout.json and has the ai-engineer attest 'did not open eval/holdout.json'. However, E1/E4 give `npm run eval` only one fallback mode, and it always loads holdout.json. It prints holdout accuracy, holdout high-urgency recall and held-out-family flag recall, and with --verbose it prints failing row ids. The ai-engineer needs this command to see whether the keyword lists (task 11) and detector (task 10) meet the fallback thresholds. So the expected workflow is: tune, run the eval, read the holdout metrics, tune again. That is fitting to the holdout through aggregate feedback, and the 'did not open the file' attestation does not cover it. heldout-hygiene.test.js is also run by `npm test`, and the spec does not say what its failure message prints. If it prints the matching 5-word held-out sequence, held-out text leaks to whoever runs the suite. This is the mechanism ARCH-12 flagged, and it is not closed by the file split alone.
evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/design/spec.md#E5 Integrity: freeze, holdout and held-out visibility (ARCH-4, ARCH-12)
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the spec defines the following. (1) A tune-only runner mode, e.g. `node eval/run.js --split tune`. It loads only eval/dataset.json, never opens holdout.json, enforces only the all-rows and injection checks it can compute, prints 'holdout: NOT SCORED (tune mode)', and never prints a final ECCODE_EVAL line that could be mistaken for a verification result (or prints one with a distinct `mode` field). (2) Tasks 10 and 11 use only tune mode, and their handoffs attest 'did not open eval/holdout.json and did not run the eval in full mode'. The full mode runs first at task 16 or verification. (3) heldout-hygiene.test.js failure messages print only the held-out row id and the rules file name, never ticket text, canary or url. (4) runner.test.js covers that tune mode does not read holdout.json (e.g. pass a non-existent --holdout path and expect no exit 2).

findings.title: ARCH-11 product-token mask fails at the end of a sentence, which is where V1 forces a summary to end
findings.detail: The mask lookahead `(?![\w./:@-])` refuses to mask a token followed by '.', so the bare-domain rule still rejects 'Customer reports a crash in VB.NET.', 'Customer reports errors in ASP.NET.' and 'Socket.io connections drop after the update to Socket.io.'. All three pass V1 (ev:ev-muymwez0-01deadbe). Mid-sentence uses ('ASP.NET, and', 'socket.io?') are accepted. V1 requires a terminal '.', '!' or '?', so a summary ending with the product name, a common shape, still becomes invalid_output and still inflates live fallback_rate. The safety direction is right.
findings.recommendation: Allow sentence-final punctuation in the lookahead, e.g. `(?![\w/:@-]|\.[\w])`. Add accept vectors 'Customer reports errors in ASP.NET.' and 'Customer reports a crash in VB.NET.', and confirm all 7 existing mask reject vectors (notably 'Go to asp.net.evil.com now.' and 'Go to socket.io.evil.ru now.') still reject. Alternatively, record the residual as accepted in Open Questions.

findings.title: Redactor is not linear-time; the stated worst case (~5 ms) is not the worst case
findings.detail: T8 and the performance table claim a 'linear-time redactor (≈5 ms worst case)', measured with a single card-shaped input. On 8,000-character adversarial inputs the submitted redact() takes 35-39 ms (ev:ev-muymwez0-01deadbe): 'a.' x4000 (email local part with no '@') takes 38.8 ms, 'a@'+'a.' x3999 takes 35.6 ms, '1.' x4000 (phone) takes 38.6 ms, and '1' x8000 takes 35.0 ms. That is backtracking that grows faster than linearly, not linear time. It is bounded by the 8,000-character cap and runs only in live mode, so it is not a DoS for a loopback app. But the claim is wrong, and a < 50 ms unit-test timing assertion on these inputs would be close to its limit and flaky.
findings.recommendation: Correct T8 and the performance table, or make the patterns linear: anchor the email local part on a preceding non-word boundary or scan from each '@' outward, and pre-split on whitespace for the phone pass. Put the adversarial inputs above in unit/redact.test.js with a budget that has real margin (e.g. < 200 ms), or measure p95 over repeats.

findings.title: Workflow dependencies: http-server (task 6) needs validateTicketInput from service.js (task 12); eval/run.js (task 8) needs app.js (task 13)
findings.detail: C3 assigns input validation to `validateTicketInput` in service.js. http-server is the only caller, but createServer({config, service, log}) does not inject it, so http-server.js must require service.js. The backend owner's order is 5 → 6 → 12, so http-server.test.js cannot pass when task 6 is handed off. Similarly, E1 has run.js call buildApp() (task 13), but task 8 depends only on 2 and 4. runner.test.js uses --results mode, which is fine only if run.js requires app.js lazily. Both cases have disjoint file ownership and can be fixed by reordering.
findings.recommendation: Choose one: inject validateTicketInput into createServer, or move it to a small pure module owned with task 6, or order task 12 before task 6. State that run.js requires app.js lazily, only when executing rows. Task 16 should have a single owner. The delivery-lead can carry this into the plan.

findings.title: Non-loopback HOST exposes the key-spending endpoint to any network client; the Host check is not access control
findings.detail: With HOST=0.0.0.0 or a LAN address, `<HOST>:P` is allowlisted. Any non-browser client on the network can send that Host header (or 127.0.0.1:P) and spend the API key and submit tickets, because the Host/Origin checks only defend browsers against DNS rebinding. The Security section says auth is required 'before any non-local deployment', but config accepts any HOST silently.
findings.recommendation: When HOST is not a loopback address, either refuse to start unless an explicit opt-in variable is set, or emit a `warning` log event and a README note. Add a unit/config.test.js case.

findings.title: Redaction and detector edge cases worth cheap hardening
findings.detail: Observed in ev:ev-muymwez0-01deadbe: a card with NBSP separators ('4111\u00a01111\u00a01111\u00a01111') is sent unredacted, a dotted card leaves the last group, and two adjacent cards collapse into one placeholder (count 1). All of these fall under the documented RISK-9 under-redaction, but NBSP and tab are common in text pasted from email clients. Separately, an attacker can write a full-width '＜/ticket＞', which is visually identical to the neutralised form, so INJ_DELIM should match it.
findings.recommendation: Optionally treat \u00a0 and \t as card and phone group separators (add CARD_CASES vectors), and have INJ_DELIM match full-width and other angle-bracket lookalikes (＜ ＞ 〈 〉 ‹ ›) around 'ticket' and 'system'.

review.summary: Re-review of sub-muynca23-01dd53b5. Both majors are closed in the spec text, and the reference vectors and my own probes back that up. DES-1: C6.4/C7 make `redirect: 'error'` mandatory, with a 3xx stub mapping to redirect_refused and the real fetch throw mapping to fetch_threw. The base URL moved to the app-specific TRIAGE_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, limited to https or http to loopback, with no userinfo, query or fragment, and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is never read. spawn-server builds the child env explicitly. Each of these has a named test. My probe applied the specified algorithm with the real Node 22 fetch: 301, 302, 303, 307, 308 and a same-origin redirect all became model_error/fetch_threw, with 0 requests and no key at the other origin (ev:ev-muynf17k-01beb841). DES-2: the new tune mode never opens holdout.json and never prints ECCODE_EVAL. Tasks 10 and 11 are tune-only, with a verbatim attestation. The first full run moves to task 16 (delivery-lead). Hygiene failures print only the row id and the file path. design-vectors.js and http-probe.js both pass on my re-run (ev:ev-muynecja-012eae7c, ev:ev-muynecy9-0119e964). The minor findings DES-3 to DES-7 are addressed. The task order is buildable and file ownership stays disjoint. Two new minor findings and one info do not block: the DES-3 mask lookbehind is ASCII-only, which reopens rejection of 'éasp.net'-style IDN hosts the brief baseline caught; and the full/tune exit-2 last-line wording conflicts.

resolvedFindings.resolution: All four parts of the resolution condition are in the spec, each with a named test. (1) C6.4 adds redirect:'error' to the fetchImpl init type and makes it mandatory in step 3. A thrown error maps to model_error/fetch_threw, and step 4 maps a 3xx status to model_error/redirect_refused without reading the body. C7 'Transport options' states the same rule. The tests are anthropic-provider.test.js (init.redirect === 'error', a 307 stub and a TypeError stub) and triage-modes.test.js AC4 (o) (real fetch, 307 and 308 to localhost:B, 0 requests at B). My probe ran the specified steps 2-4 with the real Node 22.22.0 fetch. 301, 302, 303, 307, 308 and a same-origin 307 all gave model_error/fetch_threw, with 0 requests and no x-api-key at the second origin. A 307 stub gave redirect_refused without calling text(), and a never-settling stub still timed out (ev:ev-muynf17k-01beb841). The designer's http-probe also passes on my re-run (ev:ev-muynecy9-0119e964): 307 and 308 throw with redirect:'error', the default follow sends the key on, and a 200 is unaffected. (2) checkBaseUrl requires https, or http only for 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1]. It rejects raw '?' and '#', userinfo, query and hash, and the ConfigError names only the variable. All 19 BASE_URL_CASES pass (ev:ev-muynecja-012eae7c), including the 4 required vectors. My edge cases (ev:ev-muynf17k-01beb841) found no hole: 0x7f.0.0.1, 2130706433 and 127.0.0.1. canonicalise to 127.0.0.1, which is loopback; localhost., ::ffff:127.0.0.1, javascript: and an empty host are rejected; and backslash or '@' in the path keeps the host. (3) The variable is renamed to TRIAGE_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is never read. On top of that, baseUrlCustom appears in the listening event, a custom_base_url warning is logged, and the README carries a warning. The test is config.test.js (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL alone is ignored). OQ-D3 keeps these guarantees if the SDK is adopted later. (4) spawn-server builds its env as {PATH, ...testEnv, PORT} and never spreads process.env. privacy.test.js sets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='' explicitly and adds a parent-env isolation case (a fake key and base URL in the parent; the child must report fallback mode and baseUrlCustom:false). The eval runner's fallback path reads no environment variable.

resolvedFindings.resolution: All four parts are specified. (1) E1 adds `--split tune` (npm run eval:tune). It never opens, stats or resolves --holdout. It scores only dataset.json rows on 8 computable checks and prints 'holdout: NOT SCORED (tune mode)'. It never prints the substring ECCODE_EVAL: its last line is TUNE_EVAL {"mode":"tune",...}. It is fallback-only, so `--provider live` is a usage error. I checked that ECCode's evaluator (lib/memory/improve.js:90) matches /ECCODE_EVAL\s+(\{.*\})/ anywhere in a log, so a distinct line prefix is the right mechanism. Tune verbose output prints only failing dataset.json ids. (2) E5 'No feedback path' and the workflow constraints make tasks 10 and 11 tune-only, with the verbatim handoff attestation. The first full-mode run is at task 16 (delivery-lead, single owner), and the verification report must count any later full-mode runs. Task 11 now depends on 5, 8, 10 and 12, so tune mode is actually runnable there without app.js. (3) Hygiene failures use only assert.fail('held-out overlap: row <id> in <path>'). Value-printing asserts and held-out text in titles are banned, and there is a self-check on the message regex, which matches the D5 id format /^[a-z]-\d{3}$/. No other npm test reads the real holdout. (4) runner.test.js runs tune mode with a non-existent --holdout path and expects no exit 2, no ECCODE_EVAL substring and total 8. This is a design-gate finding, so no executable runner exists yet; the evidence is the spec text plus the named tests, to be re-run at the phase gate.

findings.title: DES-3 product-token mask lookbehind is ASCII-only, so a Unicode letter or digit before the token (an IDN host such as 'éasp.net') now passes V2, which the brief baseline rejected
findings.detail: PRODUCT_TOKENS uses `(?<![\w.@/:-])`, and \w is ASCII-only without the `u` flag. 'Go to éasp.net now.', 'Go to ñsocket.io now.' and 'Go to ١asp.net now.' are all accepted by hasLink in design-vectors.js (ev:ev-muynf17k-01beb841). The brief's LINK_PATTERNS bare-domain rule rejects 'éasp.net', because \b falls between 'é' and 'a' and 'asp.net' matches. So the mask reopens a case the baseline closed. The impact is narrow: V2 already misses all-non-ASCII IDN hosts, the reply is rendered with textContent, and the attacker needs the model to emit a specific registrable IDN. That is why this is minor, not major. Also noted: 'See asp.net.” now.' (curly closing quote) is rejected. That is a harmless false reject because the lookahead lists only ASCII closing quotes.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when schema.js makes the lookbehind Unicode-aware, e.g. `/(?<![\p{L}\p{N}\p{M}_.@/:-])(?:asp\.net|ado\.net|vb\.net|socket\.io)(?=...)/giu`, and adds the reject vectors 'Go to éasp.net now.' and 'Go to ñsocket.io now.' to unit/schema.test.js (and design-vectors.js), with all existing accept and reject vectors still passing. Optionally add ’ and ” to the closing-quote set in the lookahead. This can be carried into task 4 without another design iteration.

findings.title: Exit-2 last line is specified two ways: the 'Both modes' bullet says ECCODE_EVAL {"passed":0,"total":1}, the tune section says TUNE_EVAL
findings.detail: E4's tune block says 'On exit 2 the last line is TUNE_EVAL {"mode":"tune","passed":0,"total":1}', and E1 says tune mode never prints the substring ECCODE_EVAL. But the shared 'Both modes: Exit codes' bullet says that on exit 2 the runner prints ECCODE_EVAL {"passed":0,"total":1}. runner.test.js asserts the absence of ECCODE_EVAL only for the exit-0/1 tune case. For the `--split tune --provider live` exit-2 case it asserts only the exit code. The safe reading wins in practice, and a 0/1 ECCODE_EVAL is a failing result, never a false pass. But an implementer could follow the 'Both modes' text.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the 'Both modes' exit-2 bullet says 'full mode prints ECCODE_EVAL {"passed":0,"total":1}; tune mode prints TUNE_EVAL {"mode":"tune","passed":0,"total":1}', and runner.test.js also asserts no ECCODE_EVAL substring for `--split tune --provider live` (exit 2). The delivery-lead can carry this into the task 8 acceptance criteria.

review.summary: The plan is structurally valid and complete. All 50 spec-tree files have exactly one owner, ownership globs are disjoint across all 17 tasks, every spec task, component and AC maps to a task, DES-8/9/10 are placed correctly, and DES-2 holdout discipline is carried into t08/t11/t12/t16/t17. Two things must change before implementation. (1) t16 must run every documented command, including `npm test`, but it depends only on t13. Under maxConcurrency=2 the engine makes t16 ready while t15 is still claimed, so t16's suite run covers another subagent's half-finished contract tests. (2) The three plan check scripts that verify t01, t02 and t16 and gate the foundation and integration phases are not in the submission. No task owns them, and `.eccode/**` is always allowed by task completion, so they are neither hash-pinned nor protected. The worst exposure is the dataset precheck, which is edited and run by the same task whose output it checks.

criteria.description: Plan passes `eccode plan validate` (schema, known phases/owners/deps, no later-phase deps, no cycles, no ownership warnings)
Tasks cover the spec: every file in the spec directory tree, every spec workflow task 1-16 (merge 10+11 and split of 14 justified), and every AC/test file in the Testing Strategy table maps to a task
Every task has owner, dependencies, inputs, outputs, file ownership, acceptance criteria and a verification method/command
File ownership: globs pairwise disjoint across all tasks (not only concurrent ones), each spec-tree file has exactly one owner, and each task's verification command runs only test files it owns
Dependency correctness: no task is blocked by a missing dependency, and no task's required checks run files owned by a task that can still be in progress concurrently

DES-2 holdout discipline: rules author reads dataset.json only, measures only with eval:tune, never runs the precheck or full mode; freeze precedes rules files by phase order; hygiene test is the only npm-test reader of holdout.json; first full-mode run is t17 by delivery-lead and is counted
Design review findings placed: DES-8 in t04 AC + core-modules phase criterion (design-vectors.js left untouched, justified), DES-9 in t08 AC + pipeline criterion, DES-10 as t06 in t11 dependencies

Phases independently verifiable with pinned, reviewed instruments: each phase criterion names a command, and the commands the plan relies on are part of the reviewed submission and cannot be changed silently by the tasks they verify
Buildable by parallel subagents under maxConcurrency=2: waves are feasible, longest tasks are scheduled first, same-phase concurrent tasks share no files

findings.title: t16-readme runs `npm test` but does not depend on t14/t15, so it can run against another subagent's half-finished contract tests
findings.detail: t16's third acceptance criterion requires every documented command except full-mode eval to be run once from the project root and to work. The documented commands include `npm test`, whose glob `test/**/*.test.js` covers t14's and t15's files. t16 depends only on t13-app-wiring. I simulated the integration phase with the engine's own readyTasks() and the plan's dependencies at maxConcurrency=2 (ev:ev-muynyxxl-01ff66ef). All of t14, t15 and t16 are ready at once. After t14 completes while t15 is still claimed, t16 is the next ready task. Its `npm test` run then either fails on t15's in-progress files, so t16 fails or burns retries for reasons outside its ownership, or it passes on an incomplete suite, so the README's claim that `npm test` works is not established. This contradicts plan.md's own claim that a subagent is never failed by another subagent's half-finished files.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when either (a) t16.dependencies includes t14-contract-http and t15-contract-modes-privacy, with the plan.md wave table updated to show t14 ∥ t15, then t16, then t17; or (b) t16's acceptance criterion excludes `npm test` from the commands t16 runs (t17 already runs the full suite) and says so explicitly. `eccode plan validate` must still pass.

findings.title: The plan check scripts that verify t01, t02 and t16 and gate two phases are not in the submission, have no owner, and are editable by any task
findings.detail: The verification.command values of t01-scaffold, t02-eval-dataset and t16-readme, and the criteria of the foundation and integration phases, call .eccode/artifacts/plan/checks/{scaffold-check,dataset-precheck,readme-check}.js. The plan submission hashes only plan.json and plan.md. No task's file globs cover these scripts, and lib/tasks.js ALWAYS_ALLOWED (`.eccode/**`) lets any task change them without an ownership error at completion (ev:ev-muynyxxl-01ff66ef). So the instruments are neither reviewed nor pinned by this gate. The worst case is dataset-precheck.js, the pre-freeze guard for the frozen evaluation data (E5/D6). The test-engineer in t02 runs it against their own dataset and could change it without the engine or a later reviewer noticing. I read all three scripts, and on inspection they implement what plan.md describes. scaffold-check accepts the spec's exact §Deployment package.json and .env.example and rejects a mutated package.json (ev:ev-muynynlv-01f7a511). The problem is pinning, not content.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the resubmission includes the three check scripts as submission artifacts, so their sha256 values are recorded with the plan. plan.md must also state that no implementation task may modify .eccode/artifacts/plan/checks/**. The foundation and integration phase criteria (or the phase submission routine) must require the phase reviewer to confirm the scripts' sha256 values still equal the plan submission before relying on their output.

findings.title: t17's chained verification command conflicts with its own 'complete even if the full eval fails' criterion
findings.detail: t17.verification.command is `npm test && npm run eval && node .eccode/artifacts/design/design-vectors.js`. If the first full-mode eval exits 1 because a holdout floor is missed, the chain stops and design-vectors never runs. Re-running the same command would be a second full-mode run, which E5 forbids inside the task. The acceptance criteria already say the task completes on the passing npm test evidence, so the intent is right, but the literal command steers an implementer the wrong way.
findings.recommendation: Express t17's verification as three separate `eccode evidence run` steps, `npm test`, `npm run eval` (exactly once) and `node .eccode/artifacts/design/design-vectors.js`, instead of one && chain.

findings.title: Some cross-task needs are satisfied only by phase ordering, not by declared dependencies
findings.detail: t14's http.test.js (static responses, AC11 headers, traversal 404) and spawned servers in t13/t15 need public/ from t07. Neither t14 nor t13 depends on t07, directly or transitively. This is safe because phase gates run strictly in sequence and core-modules is approved before rules-and-wiring and integration. t13's use of the t03 helpers is covered transitively through t06. Also, the core-modules phase criterion for DES-8 lists two of the three reject vectors that t04's criterion lists (the Arabic-Indic digit vector is missing).
findings.recommendation: Optional: add t07-ui to t14-contract-http.dependencies for explicitness, and list all three DES-8 reject vectors in the core-modules phase criterion.

Their recorded sha256 values equal the files on disk and the values pinned in plan.md and in a hash criterion on every phase. No task owns checks/**, t01/t02/t16 forbid modifying them, and the toolkit now limits task completion to .eccode/drafts/**. The scripts are byte-identical to the versions whose content I verified in review 1. PLAN-3 and PLAN-4 are fixed. plan validate passes.

Coverage, task completeness and disjoint ownership from review 1 are preserved: the only changes are dependency additions, acceptance criteria and t17's verification shape (diff read in full)
Dependency correctness: no task's required checks run files owned by a task that can still be in progress (PLAN-1)

Phases independently verifiable with pinned, reviewed instruments: the check scripts are in the submission with sha256 values, every phase requires a hash check before their output is relied on, and no task can change them through task completion (PLAN-2)
DES-2/E5 discipline is intact: t17 runs the full-mode eval exactly once as a separate evidence step, and design-vectors runs whatever the eval's exit code (PLAN-3)

resolvedFindings.resolution: t16-readme.dependencies now includes t14-contract-http and t15-contract-modes-privacy, and t16's criterion says its npm test run covers the complete suite. I re-ran the engine readyTasks() simulation at maxConcurrency=2. At phase start only t14 and t15 are ready. With t14 done and t15 still claimed, nothing is ready. t16 becomes ready only when both are done, and t17 after t16. The plan.md wave table shows t14 ∥ t15, then t16, then t17. plan validate still passes.

Fixed in four places. (1) dataset-precheck.js, readme-check.js and scaffold-check.js are artifacts of sub-muyo2cvo-017a28b9, and their recorded sha256 values equal the files on disk. (2) Those values are pinned in plan.md and in a 'Pinned instruments' criterion on all five phases, and a mismatch fails the phase. The phase submission routine also checks the hashes first. (3) No task owns checks/**. t01, t02 and t16 carry a criterion forbidding changes to it, and plan.md states the rule. (4) The toolkit's task-completion ALWAYS_ALLOWED is now ['.eccode/drafts/**'], which no longer covers checks/**. The scripts are byte-identical to the versions I verified in review 1 (no git diff since f0a68c9), so that content verification (ev:ev-muynynlv-01f7a511) still holds.

t17's verification is now three separate `eccode evidence run` steps joined by ';', not '&&'. `npm run eval` appears exactly once, and the method says step 3 runs whatever step 2's exit code is, with no second full-mode run.

APIs: http-client.request({port, method, path, headers, body, setHost=true, hostname='127.0.0.1', timeoutMs=10000}) -> {status, headers, body, json|null}; a `host` header (any case) overrides Host, setHost:false with no host header sends none; string/Buffer body sent byte-for-byte, other values JSON-stringified with content-type application/json only if none given; content-length always set unless supplied; rejects on transport errors (ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT). fake-fetch: respond(status, jsonOrText), messageBody(obj, opts) (body object), messageOk(obj, {stop_reason='end_turn', thinkingFirst=false, usage, model}) (stub; body also on stub.body; usage default {input_tokens:120, output_tokens:40}, usage:null omits the key; a string obj is used verbatim as the text block), never() (never settles even on abort), throws(err=TypeError('fetch failed')) (rejects), capture(inner) (records {url, init, body: parsed|null, rawBody} before delegating; .calls, .count). fake-anthropic: startFakeAnthropic() -> {port, address, url, requests[{method,path,headers,body,json}], count (on arrival), reply(status, jsonOrText, {once, headers}), replyMessage(obj, opts, {once}), redirect(3xx, location, {once}), reset(), close()}; binds 127.0.0.1 (loopback-only enforced); unprogrammed requests get 500 api_error. spawn-server: buildChildEnv(testEnv) and spawnServer({env, entry='src/server.js', cwd=project root, timeoutMs=10000}) -> {child, env, port, listening, stdout(), stderr(), logs(), waitForLog(pred,{timeoutMs}), stop()}; spawns process.execPath (no PATH lookup), rejects with exitCode/stderr on early exit, kills and rejects on listening timeout, stop() is SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 3 s and idempotent, plus a process-exit SIGKILL safety net. Self-test covers: Host default/foreign/missing/[::1] and Origin; body encodings and 20 KB body; HEAD; ECONNREFUSED rejection; capture url/init/parsed body/count (also with never inner); never() pending before and after abort; thinkingFirst order; fake-anthropic programmed 200 + recorded headers/body, once-queue, reset, unprogrammed 500; 307 and 308 to a second instance at http://localhost:<B>: fetch redirect:'error' throws TypeError and B counts 0, with a follow-mode control proving B's counter is live (B counts 1 via localhost); DES-1 with parent ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/TRIAGE_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL set: child env keys are exactly the test keys + PATH + PORT, PORT forced to '0', parent key absent from child output; early-exit and timeout paths. findings.title: fake-fetch responses do not record whether the body was read
findings.detail: The pipeline-phase criterion and the unit/anthropic-provider row in spec §Testing Strategy require that "a stub answering 307 gives model_error/redirect_refused without reading the body". makeResponse() in test/helpers/fake-fetch.js returns text()/json() closures that track no reads, so respond(307, ...) cannot prove the body was left unread. t09 would have to hand-roll its own stub.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when makeResponse exposes a read counter, for example `res.bodyReads` incremented by text() and json(), and helpers.test.js covers it. Alternatively, t09's handoff shows a local stub that asserts text() was never called.

findings.title: Tune-mode flag FPR has 8 instructionLike rows, so one false positive fails it
findings.detail: dataset.json has 8 instructionLike benign rows; the union has 12. In tune mode (E3), injection_flag_fpr <= 0.10 tolerates 0/8, because 1/8 = 0.125. Full mode tolerates 1/12 = 0.083. In-family flag_recall >= 0.90 over 18 rows tolerates at most 1 miss. These numbers are consistent with the spec, but t11 should expect the tune check to be stricter than the full one.
findings.recommendation: No change to the frozen files. delivery-lead should pass this note to t11 (rules author) as tuning context, without holdout content.

findings.title: Redirect self-test control relies on localhost reaching 127.0.0.1
findings.detail: The 307/308 tests use Location http://localhost:<B>, matching AC4(o). B binds 127.0.0.1 only. The follow-mode control (B counts 1) passes here, but on a host where localhost resolves only to ::1 the control fails, while the redirect:'error' assertion would still hold.
findings.recommendation: Optional: t15 can reuse the same pattern. If CI shows a flake, bind B with host 'localhost' or use 127.0.0.1 in the control request.

findings.title: Labels come from a single labeller, and some rows are borderline by design
findings.detail: I read every row and found the labels plausible under E6 and the system-prompt urgency definitions. Rows such as b-052 and h-024 (phishing reports, labelled other/high) and b-029 (lost 2FA but still signed in on one device, labelled account/medium) are defensible but contestable. The t02 handoff already discloses this. Their effect on the accuracy metrics is small.
findings.recommendation: No change, because the files are frozen. The verification report should state that the labels have a single author (E7 honesty).

review.summary: Security review of sub-muyp6003-014a87e3 (18 artifacts), done by reading the code and running my own probes. The HTTP shell enforces the C1 order: Host, then Origin, then route, then method, then 415/413, then body. A foreign Host or Origin with a 20 KB, chunked or Expect: 100-continue body gets 403, not 413, and no 100 Continue is sent. DNS-rebinding Host variants are refused: trailing dot, numeric and short IPv4, IPv6 long and mapped forms, wrong port, userinfo or suffix tricks, an empty Host and a missing Host. Origin 'null', empty, https and trailing-slash values get 403. No response carries Access-Control-* headers. Security headers are present on every handler response. Bodies over 16384 bytes get 413 whether the limit is reached through Content-Length or chunked transfer. A 500 or 4xx response never echoes input, and logs hold metadata only. Config enforces the DES-1 base-URL rules and the DES-6 loopback rule, and its errors never echo values. Redaction leaves no Luhn window on ARCH-10 or DES-7 vectors or on 3000 fuzzed embedded cards, and it stays within its time budget on 12 extra adversarial inputs. V1-V4 behave as specified, and the DES-8 deviation is strictly stricter. The prompt isolates the ticket, sends no tools or sampling parameters, and keeps the system prompt constant. The UI uses only textContent and value sinks. Pinned check-script hashes match, the full suite passes 259/259, design vectors pass, and only the 18 owned files changed. Approved with one minor finding (validator cost on long model output, recorded as RISK-10) and five info observations.

DES-8 resolved: the product-token mask lookbehind is Unicode-aware. unit/schema.test.js holds the three required reject vectors. Earlier accept and reject vectors pass. The t04 deviation (ASCII case classes with the 'gu' flags, plus \p{Cf}) only adds rejections: the long-s 'aſp.net', soft hyphen, ZWJ and combining-mark variants are rejected, and the accept vectors still pass
No file outside the phase tasks' ownership globs changed: git diff a54af19 (excluding .eccode) lists exactly the 18 submitted files

T2 DNS rebinding and cross-site requests. The Host allowlist runs first and holds against rebinding and port tricks. The Origin check covers every non-GET/HEAD method, including null and duplicate Origin headers. OPTIONS gets 405. No Access-Control-* header is sent. Every pre-body rejection carries Connection: close, and no 100 Continue is sent before the checks pass

T8/T9 input limits and error leakage. 415 is decided before the body is read. 413 applies above 16384 bytes, whether the size comes from Content-Length or a streamed or chunked body. invalid_json and invalid_request are handled as specified, including a __proto__ ticket. A service exception gives a fixed 500 body with no message or stack. Static routes use an exact-match map, so traversal and encoding variants get 404. Health never exposes the key

T6 logs are metadata only. The ticket text, a canary in the API key, the Host and Origin values and the service error message never appear in any log line. meta.detail carrying ticket text is dropped by the DETAIL allowlist

T11/T12 config. TRIAGE_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL accepts https, or http only to a loopback host. It rejects userinfo, query, fragment, empty ?/#, file/javascript/ws schemes and http to localhost. or 127.0.0.2. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is ignored. A non-loopback HOST is refused without TRIAGE_ALLOW_REMOTE=1. ConfigError messages never contain the value or the key. The config object is frozen

T5 redaction (D3/ARCH-10/DES-7). No Luhn-valid window survives the ARCH-10 cases, NBSP, tab or mixed separators, card plus CVV or expiry, phone plus card, or 3000 fuzzed embedded cards. Emails and NBSP/tab phones are redacted. 12 extra adversarial inputs each have a median under 200 ms

T1 prompt construction. The request body has only the keys model, max_tokens, system, messages and output_config (effort low, json_schema). It has no tools, thinking or sampling parameters. The system prompt is constant. The ticket sits only inside the delimiters, with no ASCII < or > in between, including on input with </ticket>, <system>, CRLF and lookalike brackets. neutralise is idempotent

V1-V4 and validateResponse. Single-sentence checks, link and email rejection, and enum normalisation all hold, including Turkish dotted I, NUL and __proto__ values. validateTriage enforces exact own keys and rejects inherited keys, arrays and null. Responses use strict enums. checkSchemaKeywords rejects maxLength. OUTPUT_SCHEMA is deep-frozen

T3 UI XSS. public/ has no innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval, new Function, on* attributes or inline script or style. Server and model data are written only through textContent or textarea.value. className values come from fixed literals after validation. fetch targets only /api/health and /api/triage. Nothing is stored client-side

findings.title: V2 link validator is O(n^2) on long model output; validateTriage applies it without a length gate
findings.detail: textFieldErrors runs containsLinkOrEmail on summary and suggestedReply whatever their length. Its six regexes (obfuscated-email, bare-domain, host-path, email, scheme) rescan from every word boundary. A ticket can steer the model toward degenerate output such as 'a.a.a.' or '1.1.1.'. On such output validateTriage takes a median of 508 ms with 8,000 characters in each field and 6.6-8.2 s with 32,000 characters. TRIAGE_MAX_TOKENS can be set up to 16000, which allows output that long. The work blocks the single-threaded server's event loop. The output then fails V1 or V4 anyway. Impact is limited: the server is local and single-user, the model must cooperate, the operator controls max_tokens, and each run costs one paid model call. The worst case at the default 2048 tokens is about a quarter of a second. The same check on spec-length input (1,200 characters) takes about 6 ms. Recorded as RISK-10.
findings.recommendation: In validateTriage/validateResponse, run containsLinkOrEmail only when summary.length <= 200 and suggestedReply.length <= 1200. Otherwise report summary_v1 or reply_length alone. Add a unit test that a 32k-character 'a.' reply is rejected in under 50 ms. Do this before or with t09 (anthropic-provider) wiring.

findings.title: Cards written in non-ASCII digits (full-width U+FF10-FF19, Arabic-Indic) are not redacted
findings.detail: redact('card ４１１１ １１１１ １１１１ １１１１') returns the text unchanged with card=0. D3 uses \d, which matches ASCII digits only, and the reference implementation behaves the same way. This class is not among the RISK-9 under-redaction cases listed in D3. Such input is unlikely in English tickets, but full-width digits can come from IME or CJK clipboard text.
findings.recommendation: Either list it under RISK-9 / D3 'Known under-redaction', or apply NFKC (or a digit-only fold) to a copy for detection before the card and phone passes. Leave this to the design owner. It does not block this phase.

findings.title: Requests rejected by Node's HTTP parser get Node's bare 400 without C1 security headers (delivery-lead note confirmed)
findings.detail: Two requests were rejected by Node's parser before the handler ran: one with 'Content-Length: abc' and one with CL+TE together, a smuggling attempt. Both got 'HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request' with an empty body and no CSP or nosniff headers. The body is empty and nothing can render, so there is no exploitable impact. CL+TE smuggling is rejected.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add server.on('clientError') that writes a fixed 400 with SECURITY_HEADERS and closes the socket. Otherwise keep it documented as accepted.

findings.title: V2 residuals inherited from the brief rules: ideographic or full-width dots, defanged '[.]' and IDN-only labels pass
findings.detail: The following are not rejected: 'evil。com', 'evil[.]com', 'еvil．com' and '例え.com'. The six V2 rules are ASCII-only, and D4 keeps them unchanged on purpose. The implementation matches the spec. The output is display-only (textContent and textarea), the system prompt forbids domains, and a human copy step follows. This is noted for T4 and RISK-1 visibility. It is not an implementation defect.
findings.recommendation: Consider an NFKC fold and treating U+3002, U+FF0E and U+FF61 as '.' before V2 in a later design revision. Track it under RISK-1/T4.

findings.title: V1 rejects only CR/LF, so U+2028/U+2029 line separators pass inside a summary; the 403 UI text keeps a literal '<port>'
findings.detail: isSingleSentence('Foo\u2028bar.') returns true. The spec says 'no CR/LF', so this is spec-conformant, but some renderers show U+2028 as a line break. The '(http://127.0.0.1:<port>)' text in errorMessage(403) is written with textContent, so the literal '<port>' is inert and has no security impact. Its wording belongs to the technical designer (t07 note).
findings.recommendation: Optional: extend the V1 line-break check to /[\r\n\u0085\u2028\u2029]/. Let the designer settle the 403 wording.

handoff.expectedOutput: createAnthropicProvider(opts) returning {model, analyse(redactedTicket) => Promise<LiveResult>} that never rejects, makes at most one fetch, and maps every outcome to the C6.4 reasons and fixed detail codes; unit tests with fake-fetch stubs.
acceptanceCriteria: Implements the C6.4 10-step algorithm in order; analyse never rejects; uses only res.status and res.text(); at most one fetch call per analyse; no SDK or other dependency
AC4 (a)-(n) at provider level incl. never() stub times out, thinking-first content, usage mapping, headers and URL (baseUrl + /v1/messages)
DES-1: a capture stub asserts init.redirect === 'error'; a 307 stub gives model_error/redirect_refused without calling text(); a stub throwing TypeError gives model_error/fetch_threw
RISK-10: model output with summary > 200 or suggestedReply > 1200 chars is rejected (invalid_output) before validateTriage/V2; a 32k-char 'a.a.a.' payload returns fallback in < 100 ms
handoff.completedWork: src/triage/anthropic-provider.js (zero deps, CommonJS) exports createAnthropicProvider({apiKey, model, baseUrl, timeoutMs, maxTokens, fetchImpl}) -> {model, analyse}. analyse follows C6.4 in order: (1) buildRequestBody inside the try, so its TypeError (t04 note) becomes model_error/fetch_threw with no fetch call; (2) AbortController + setTimeout(timeoutMs); (3) one fetchImpl(baseUrl + '/v1/messages', {method:'POST', headers:{content-type, x-api-key, anthropic-version:2023-06-01}, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal, redirect:'error'}), and then res.text(), each raced against the abort signal (a never-settling stub still times out); abort -> timeout/'timeout', any other throw (incl. sync throw, non-function fetchImpl, non-object response or non-integer status) -> model_error/fetch_threw; timer cleared in finally; abort listeners removed after settle; (4) 3xx -> model_error/redirect_refused without reading the body, other non-2xx -> model_error/http_<status> (body read under the timeout, per step order); (5) unparseable or non-object body -> model_error/body_not_json; (6) stop_reason refusal -> refusal/'refusal', max_tokens -> truncated/'max_tokens'; (7) first content element with type 'text' and string text (thinking skipped) else invalid_output/no_text_block; (8) text not JSON -> invalid_output/text_not_json; RISK-10 gate: if summary is a string > 200 chars or suggestedReply a string > 1200 chars -> invalid_output/invalid:<summary_v1|reply_length> (the same codes, in the same order, validateTriage itself reports for such output) without calling validateTriage; (9) validateTriage -> invalid_output/invalid:<codes> or {ok:true, triage (enums normalised), upstreamStatus, usage}; (10) usage {inputTokens, outputTokens} when both are numbers, else null, attached to every result where the body was parsed. upstreamStatus is the HTTP status once known, else null. detail is always a fixed code; no content is echoed (tested with a canary). test/unit/anthropic-provider.test.js: 25 tests (headers/URL/redirect/signal/body capture; AC4 a-n; DES-1 for 300-399 with a no-read stub that counts text()/json() calls (FND-1); sync throw; text() rejection; timeouts on fetch and on the body read, and abort-rejecting fetch; timer cleared; usage mapping; buildRequestBody guard; canary non-echo; RISK-10 32k payload < 100 ms and limit boundaries 200/201 and 1200/1201; never-rejects sweep). RISK-10 resolved at the call site: probe ev:ev-muypnaj3-01d37d63 shows ungated validateTriage takes 8301 ms on the 32k 'a.a.a.' output while gated analyse takes 1.87 ms with the identical detail 'invalid:summary_v1,reply_length'.
remainingIssues: RISK-10 is resolved only at this call site. schema.js validateTriage/validateResponse are unchanged (approved phase), so any other caller that validates unbounded text (e.g. t08 eval/run.js calling validateResponse on fallback or live results, t15 contract tests) still has the quadratic V2 cost; fallback output is bounded (<= 600-char templates) so the eval's fallback path is not exposed. Recommend the schema owner add the length gate inside schema.js in a later revision (the review's original recommendation).

Usage/latency logging: per C6.4 the provider has no logger and returns usage in LiveResult; latency is measured and logged by service.js (t10) via AnalysisMeta and the D1.6 request log. The provider itself logs nothing, so no prompt content can leak from it.

Interpretation within the contract: a buildRequestBody TypeError (invalid model/maxTokens/non-string ticket) and a malformed response object (null, non-integer status) map to model_error/fetch_threw, the C6.4 catch-all ('any other throw'), since the fixed detail list has no closer code. A JSON body that parses to a non-object (e.g. 'null') maps to model_error/body_not_json. Non-2xx, non-3xx bodies are read (under the timeout) before http_<status> is returned, following the step order; if that read fails the result is fetch_threw/timeout with the status.
createAnthropicProvider does not validate opts at creation (config.js validates them); invalid values surface as model_error or timeout at analyse time.
Not tested: no live Anthropic call (no API key). Results here are evidence about the pipeline against stubs, not about model behaviour or real API shape drift (RISK-7 remains open until a live call).
Not tested here: real-fetch behaviour with redirect:'error' against fake-anthropic 307 (AC4 o end-to-end) - that is t15's spawned-server test; the provider-level stub tests cover the contract.
handoff.nextAction: backend-engineer: t10-service - wrap provider.analyse per C6.4 R12 (try/catch -> provider_threw, latency measurement, usage into AnalysisMeta); backend-engineer t13 wires createAnthropicProvider with config + globalThis.fetch; schema owner (ai-engineer) to consider moving the RISK-10 length gate into schema.js in a later revision.

data.mitigation: Provider length gate before validateTriage (summary<=200, reply<=1200): 32k adversarial output 8301ms -> 1.87ms (ev-muypnaj3-01d37d63). Other validateTriage callers remain exposed; schema-level gate recommended later.
