findings.title: Non-2xx error bodies are read before http_<status> is returned
findings.detail: For 4xx/5xx the provider awaits res.text() (under the timeout) before returning http_<status>. A 500/529 whose body hangs or errors is therefore reported as timeout or fetch_threw instead of http_<status> (probe case 'http 500 text rejects' -> fetch_threw, ev:ev-muyq0yvh-01ea780e). This follows the literal C6.4 step order (text() is read in step 3), so it is conformant, but the fallbackReason/detail can be less precise and a slow error body consumes the timeout budget.
findings.recommendation: Optional: return model_error/http_<status> for non-2xx without awaiting the body (or with a best-effort cancel). Resolved when a test shows a 500 with a rejecting body yields http_500. Not required for this gate.

findings.title: RISK-10 quadratic V2 still reachable through schema.js callers other than the provider
findings.detail: The length gate lives only in anthropic-provider.js. eval/metrics.js calls validateResponse and containsLinkOrEmail on every scored response; with --results the responses come from a local file and are unbounded. Inputs are local and operator-supplied, so this is a robustness issue, not an exploitable path; the live and fallback execution paths are bounded (provider gate, <=600-char templates).
findings.recommendation: Move the length gate into schema.js (validateTriage/validateResponse/containsLinkOrEmail) in a later revision, as the t09 handoff already recommends. Resolved when containsLinkOrEmail on a 300k-char string returns within a bounded time.

findings.title: Integration contract notes for t11/t13 (untested paths)
findings.detail: (a) Real-module fallback execution and npm run eval:tune exit 2 until t11 adds injection.js and fallback-provider.js. (b) The --provider live branch with a key (buildApp + USAGE line) is untested until t13 adds app.js; it calls buildApp({env, log: createLogger(() => {})}) and relies on the default fetchImpl and on service.mode === 'live'. (c) createTriageService refuses provider === undefined, so app.js must pass provider: null explicitly in fallback mode (matches C6.4/C6.5).
findings.recommendation: t13/t15: add a test running eval/run.js --provider live against fake-anthropic via TRIAGE_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (synthetic dataset, --holdout pointing at a synthetic file), and after t11 a test that npm run eval:tune exits 0 or 1. The next phase reviewer should confirm.

findings.title: Spec-silent interpretation choices accepted
findings.detail: Accepted as reasonable and content-free: non-object JSON body -> body_not_json; malformed response object or buildRequestBody TypeError -> fetch_threw; malformed LiveResult or reason 'no_api_key' from a provider -> provider_threw; RISK-10 gate reports only length codes (subset of validateTriage codes); an enforced check with n=0 fails; --results must cover every scored id; extra 'results ... sha256' header line in --results mode.

handoff.objective: Automated held-out hygiene test over the rules files (spec E5 ARCH-12, DES-2; spec task 14 hygiene part)
handoff.context: Rules from t11 (src/triage/injection.js, src/triage/fallback-provider.js) are checked against eval/holdout.json, with eval/dataset.json 5-word sequences allowed. Failure output is id-and-path only.
handoff.expectedOutput: test/eval/heldout-hygiene.test.js plus self-check fixtures under test/eval/hygiene-fixtures/
acceptanceCriteria: Fails if any held-out row's canary or url, or any lower-cased 5-word sequence of a held-out ticket not also present in a dataset.json row, appears in src/triage/injection.js or src/triage/fallback-provider.js
Every failure is raised only as assert.fail('held-out overlap: row <id> in <rules file path>'); no value-printing asserts on held-out strings; titles carry no held-out text
Self-check: a rules file seeded with a held-out 5-word sequence yields a message matching ^held-out overlap: row [a-z]-\d{3} in \S+$ exactly
Only test in npm test that reads the real eval/holdout.json; passing output contains no held-out content
handoff.completedWork: Added test/eval/heldout-hygiene.test.js. It scans every row of eval/holdout.json (holdout benign and held-out-family attack rows): it checks canary and url as case-insensitive substrings, on both the raw text and the text with backslashes removed so regex-escaped urls are caught. It also checks lower-cased 5-word sequences. Rules source is tokenized after stripping regex escapes such as \s+ and \b, so a phrase written as a regex is still detected. Sequences that occur in any eval/dataset.json ticket are allowed. There is one subtest per rules file, titled with its path. A failure is raised only as assert.fail('held-out overlap: row <id> in <path>'); any further overlapping ids go to a diagnostic that carries ids only. JSON parse errors are rethrown with a generic message so the input is never echoed. Self-check suite: (1) synthetic fixtures (hygiene-fixtures/holdout.json, dataset.json, rules-seeded-phrase.js, rules-seeded-canary.js, rules-seeded-url.js, rules-template.js) prove that the phrase, canary and url are detected with exact id-only messages, and that the dataset allowance works. (2) A real-data mutation takes a deterministic held-out-only 5-word sequence and seeds it as a regex into a temp copy of rules-template.js (under os.tmpdir, never in the repo). The unseeded template passes. In-process, the seeded file fails with a message that matches the exact regex and names the right row. The test file is then re-run as a child process (HYGIENE_CHILD=1, HYGIENE_RULES_FILES=<seeded>): that run must exit non-zero, its output must contain the id-only message, and it must contain neither the seeded sequence nor any held-out canary or url. Result against the real t11 rules: pass (6/6 tests). A separate script confirmed that the passing output contains no 5-word sequence, canary or url from any held-out row.
remainingIssues: Detection is lexical: a held-out phrase reworded, split by regex alternation or optional groups such as (?:a|b), or shortened below 5 words is not caught. It is an overlap signal, not proof of independence. The handoff attestation (E5) remains the primary control.
Regex word fragments (for example instructions? or feature[ _-]?request) tokenize into single words, so a 5-word sequence through such a construct may be missed.
Full npm test was not recorded here because backend-engineer is concurrently changing src/app.js and test/unit/app.test.js (t13). The eval test files (runner + hygiene) pass together (35/35).

Returns {config, service, server}, not listening. The per-request log line is written by http-server.js (t06) from service meta; buildApp passes the same log to it. src/server.js: main() builds the app from process.env with globalThis.fetch and a stdout logger. A ConfigError prints exactly one stderr line 'config error: <message>' (the message names the variable, never its value) and sets exit code 1; any other startup error prints 'startup error: <code|name>' and exits 1; a listen error (e.g. EADDRINUSE) prints 'listen error: <code>' and exits 1. On listen it logs listening {host, port (actual bound port, so PORT=0 works), mode, model, timeoutMs, maxTokens, baseUrlCustom}, then one warning {code} per config.warnings. SIGTERM/SIGINT: server.close() then closeIdleConnections(), exit 0 on close; an unref'd 2 s timer forces exit (code 1). test/unit/app.test.js (11 tests): buildApp shape and not listening; explicit env wins over a parent process.env key; ConfigError without echoing the value; fallback HTTP health + triage (validateResponse ok, no_api_key, one request log line, no ticket content in logs); E1 equivalence vs the reference createTriageService over 4 tickets (response and meta, latency zeroed); live in-process with capture(messageOk) (source model, URL = config.baseUrl + '/v1/messages', x-api-key, redirect 'error', email redacted before egress, request log with upstreamStatus/redactions/usage, key never logged); config values (base URL, model, max tokens) reach the provider; spawned HOST=0.0.0.0 -> exit 1, one 'config error: HOST ...' stderr line not containing 0.0.0.0, empty stdout; spawned invalid TRIAGE_TIMEOUT_MS -> no value echoed; spawned fallback -> exact listening key order/values, health 200, request log, SIGTERM -> {code 0, signal null}; spawned live via fake-anthropic (dummy key, TRIAGE_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL loopback) -> listening mode live, baseUrlCustom true, exactly one custom_base_url warning after listening, POST triage source model, fake received /v1/messages with the key and no raw email, SIGINT -> exit 0. Test-first: red run before implementation (ev:ev-muyqdta5-015d1d58). npm start smoke (ev:ev-muyqghv3-01038cad): listening line {host 127.0.0.1, mode fallback, model claude-haiku-5-5, timeoutMs 20000, maxTokens 2048, baseUrlCustom false}, GET /api/health with Host 127.0.0.1:<port> -> 200 {status ok, mode fallback, model null}, SIGTERM to the process group -> no live process within 58 ms, 0 stderr bytes. Full suite 382/382 pass (ev:ev-muyqgpjd-012ca535).
remainingIssues: npm start signal forwarding (found by the smoke runs, failed evidence ev:ev-muyqeq3m-01bde381 and ev:ev-muyqevuo-01f19e86): /bin/sh is dash, which does not exec the single command of 'sh -c node src/server.js'. When only the npm process gets SIGTERM (as some process managers do), npm signals sh, sh dies and node src/server.js is orphaned and keeps listening. Signalling the process group (terminal Ctrl-C, or kill -- -pgid) works: the server exits 0 within ~60 ms. A fix is outside this task's globs: package.json "start": "exec node src/server.js" (or running node src/server.js directly). Recommend t16 (README/package.json owner) apply it or document 'node src/server.js' for process managers.

The 2 s forced exit uses exit code 1 (spec says 'force exit after 2 s' without a code). Interpretation: a forced exit means connections were still open, so it is reported as non-zero. Not exercised by a test (would need a stalled in-flight request); the clean path (exit 0) is tested for SIGTERM and SIGINT.

In this sandbox an orphaned process lingers as a zombie until PID 1 (/process_api) reaps it, so 'kill -0' polling overstates shutdown time (~1.8 s observed). /proc state showed Z within 200 ms. Not a server issue; noted so later timing checks use /proc state, not kill -0.

Process note: files src/app.js, src/server.js and an earlier version of .eccode/drafts/t13-npm-start-smoke.js were included in commit 2423ea9 ('Demo: t12 held-out hygiene done') by the orchestrator's commit while this task was in progress. Content is this task's work; ownership unchanged.
Not tested: a real Anthropic API call (no key). The live evidence is about the wiring against fake-fetch and fake-anthropic, not about model behaviour (RISK-7 stays open).

Not tested here: AC4 (o) redirect end-to-end with real globalThis.fetch against fake-anthropic 307/308, contract/http tests via buildApp, and the AC16 outbound-body check with card/phone/</ticket> markers: these are t14/t15 contract tests. app.test.js covers email redaction before egress only.

findings.title: LINKISH scheme alternative is quadratic on long dotted/hyphenated runs
findings.detail: detectInjection on 'a.'/'a-' repeated scales O(n^2): 8.5ms@4k, 23ms@8k, 78ms@16k, 278ms@32k chars (ev:ev-muyqml2y-01be22e4). Likely cause: \b[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\/\/ in LINKISH restarts at every word boundary and scans to the end of the sentence. Bounded in production by MAX_TICKET_CHARS=8000 (~20ms worst), so not exploitable as DoS today, but the module's comment claims linear-ish cost and it would degrade if the cap were raised.
findings.recommendation: Bound the scheme run (e.g. [a-z][a-z0-9+.-]{0,31}:\/\/) and add a timing regression test on an 8000-char dotted run.

findings.title: Hygiene test is lexical only; RISK-11 npm-start orphan noted
